goals: Mechanistic: quantify how increasing soil clay fraction shifts precipitation partitioning from sub-surface drainage/recharge toward surface runoff, all else fixed
Validation (optional): check the response against physical/hydrological expectation (monotonic runoff increase, recharge decrease with clay) rather than co-located observations
key_processes: unsaturated-zone vertical drainage (recharge) governed by saturated hydraulic conductivity and matric potential

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates water partitioning (surface runoff QOVER, sub-surface drainage QDRAI/recharge, per-layer soil moisture) and soil texture is a directly configurable per-column property, so a controlled clay ladder isolates the mechanism.

answerable: clay-content control on surface-runoff vs sub-surface-drainage partitioning under fixed forcing and vegetation
sensitivity of soil-moisture profile and recharge flux to texture via ELM pedotransfer functions

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Six clay levels evenly span the requested 5–55% range at 10% steps — enough resolution to resolve the expected nonlinear (Ksat-driven) decline in drainage/recharge and rise in surface runoff, while keeping the controlled experiment small. This is a single-factor ladder, so N = number of factor levels.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Controlled / not spatial: one synthetic column per clay level, identical location proxy, identical forcing, identical vegetation and slope; only clay (and its pedotransfer-derived hydraulic properties) varies.
sampling_strategy.replication: None needed — deterministic single-column runs under identical forcing; the response curve is the result.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-clay endmember: high Ksat, expect infiltration-dominated column with maximal deep drainage/recharge and minimal surface runoff
Loamy-sand/loam range to resolve the high-conductivity end of the response curve
Mid loam range — transition zone where partitioning begins to shift
Clay-loam: expected inflection where reduced Ksat drives rising surface runoff
High-clay: low Ksat, expect runoff-dominated partitioning and suppressed recharge
High-clay endmember bounding the requested range; maximal surface runoff, minimal recharge

validation_design.target_variable: runoff/recharge partitioning (QOVER vs QDRAI, and recharge)
validation_design.observation_source: physical/hydrological expectation and pedotransfer literature (no co-located field observations in this conceptual study)
validation_design.comparison: analog — response curve checked for monotonic, physically consistent behavior (runoff↑, drainage/recharge↓ with clay); not a co-located data comparison
validation_design.metric: qualitative monotonicity + partitioning ratio (fraction of P to runoff vs drainage) per clay level

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: fixed multi-year NLDAS-2 forcing window (spanning wet+dry years), uniform synthetic soil profile, fixed vegetation/slope; only clay fraction varied 5–55%, WITH spin-up / WTD warm start so recharge and water table are equilibrated

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up (multi-year) or WTD-informed warm start per column
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and sub-surface drainage are slow states; columns cold-start at the default ~8.8 m water table with recharge ≈0 while storage fills, so without equilibration the partitioning is an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: trustworthy recharge/drainage partitioning — the primary quantity of interest

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic uniform-soil configuration with independent control of clay fraction (and, ideally, the option to hold porosity fixed)
requires_capabilities.why: The experiment requires prescribing clay 5–55% on an otherwise identical soil profile rather than sampling real SSURGO heterogeneity

requires_capabilities.capability: history output of partitioning fluxes (QOVER surface runoff, QDRAI sub-surface drainage/recharge, infiltration)
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to compute the runoff/recharge ratio per treatment

assumptions: No domain or observations provided — treated strictly as an idealized controlled experiment.

A single representative multi-year forcing window (within 1980–2018) is chosen and held identical across all six columns; it should include both wet and dry years so the partitioning result is not driven by one anomalous year.
Vegetation, slope, soil depth, and all non-clay soil attributes are held fixed across treatments.

Clay is set via ELM pedotransfer functions, which propagate to porosity, Ksat, matric potential, and the b exponent simultaneously — so 'clay effect' includes these co-varying derived properties unless porosity is explicitly held fixed.
open_questions: Should clay be varied as the only free input (letting porosity/Ksat co-vary via pedotransfer, the realistic case) or should porosity be held fixed to isolate conductivity alone?
Preferred forcing window and length, and preferred equilibration approach (multi-year spin-up vs WTD warm start)?
Is a fixed sand/silt split assumed as clay rises (e.g. sand held constant, silt as remainder), or a specific texture trajectory?
